glossary.definition: Any legal body: a university, hospital, funding agency, industry partner, laboratory, drug depot, ethics committee (IRB) or regulator.
A funding award from a funder organization. A grant can fund several studies, and a study can have several grants.
A clinical trial, identified by a study code (SDTM `STUDYID`) and optionally a registry ID (such as an NCT number).
An approved version of the study protocol. Planned visits and eligibility criteria belong to a specific version.
A change that turns one protocol version into the next. It can be substantial or non-substantial.
A planned treatment group (SDTM TA), for example Experimental or Placebo.
A phase of the study timeline, such as Screening, Treatment or Follow-up (SDTM TE).
A visit in the schedule of assessments, with its planned day and allowed window (SDTM TV).
An inclusion or exclusion criterion (SDTM TI).
A physical research location belonging to an organization.
A clinician who conducts the trial at a site.
A site's participation in a specific study, with its own site number (SDTM `SITEID`) and status.
An ethics committee decision on a protocol version for a study site.
A pseudonymized individual. Holds only sex, birth year, ethnicity, race and country. Lets the same individual be linked across studies.
A person's participation in one study at one study site (SDTM DM, `USUBJID`).
Informed consent signed by the subject for a protocol version. Amendments may require re-consent.
The method (simple, block, stratified, minimization) and its stratification factors.
A pre-generated, blinded randomization number assigned to an arm, optionally within a stratum.
The event in which a subject consumes one list entry and is assigned to an arm.
A controlled disclosure of a subject's treatment arm, with a reason (for example an emergency or SUSAR reporting).
An actual visit (scheduled or unscheduled) that the subject attended (SDTM SV).
Findings captured at visits (SDTM VS / LB).
Prior conditions and other medications (SDTM MH / CM), coded with MedDRA and WHODrug.
The actual doses of investigational product administered (SDTM EX).
Any untoward medical occurrence (SDTM AE), coded with MedDRA.
Seriousness criteria and expedited-reporting dates for an AE that is serious.
The study drug, placebo or comparator, linked to the arm it belongs to (blinded information).
A manufactured batch with an expiry date, and a labelled, blinded package dispensed to a subject.
A movement of kits from a depot to a study site.
The handing of one kit to a subject, and any later return.
A departure from the protocol at site or subject level (SDTM DV).
A question raised on a specific data value, together with its responses, until it is closed.
An application login and the role it holds, scoped to a study and/or a study site.
An immutable record of every insert or update: who, when, old and new values, and why.
Which assessments are planned at which visit of a protocol version. Compared with collected data to find missing assessments.
